# M2 direction proposal — advisory, not authorization

2026-10-18 · Astra xhigh planning support. Verified clean parent **89e271bb8f98bef413afa9c77d8ceabff67e9790**, branch `t3/m2-direction-proposal`, and the committed [brief](../tasks/M2-PREPARATION.md). Production/tests/config remain equivalent to **d9aaf6356cb320f283887922abf97ed8bdc54f59**. Stage1 is held for OS2-01; its independent consultation and correction do not depend on this proposal. Root must reconcile the eventual accepted movement/save interfaces before assigning M2. Nothing here accepts an interface, dispatches work or claims a milestone pass.

**Recommendation:** finish one earned Canopy–Basin investigation/return with readable geography, safe recovery and persistent regional content before multiplying habitats. Then make the fleet and two complete expedition strategies work through the ending. M3 supplies authored density and fuller presentation, not the missing ending or recovery system.

These are proposed connected missions, not proof of implementation or a mandatory pickup sequence. Source tiers follow the integration contract. Route dimensions, capacities and timing still require validation. Evidence IDs below disclose no canonical resolution.

**M2 versus M3:** M2 needs actual rules, sources, affordances, usable hull tradeoffs and the essential narrative/repair chain, including consequential ending actions and a resolution scene. Rough secondary art is permissible; “coming later” machinery is not. M3 fills the entire clue graph, independent foreshadowing, human perspectives, distinctive side expeditions, ecological variety and finished hull missions. Neither milestone measures ten hours by adding transit, mandatory optional hulls, delayed logs or repeat mineral shopping.

## 3. First benchmark before breadth

The [Opus R2 report][opus] and [root disposition][opus-disposition] make **OS2-04 and OS2-06 mandatory first-M2 checks**. Existing actual artifacts viewed for this proposal: Opus frames 14/27/44/48 and the historical M1 carrier passage contact sheet. Frame 48 shows the 53 m Canopy view dominated by teal water and cockpit; frame 44 shows the pale near-floor wash. These are source-attributed stills, not new play or continuous video inspection. Archives: `/tmp/siltwake-opus-stage1-r2/` and `/tmp/siltwake-m1-carrier-coordinator/passage-contact-sheet.png`. OS2-02/03/07 remain root's bounded refinements; mouse-resume, bench-finding and blocked-thrust observations remain hypotheses, not grounds for automatic input or marker changes.

**Playable scope:** workshop preparation → existing Canopy source/lab approaches → new Basin ridge at 160–175 m → C05/C06 investigation and useful salvage → alternate return/store/save/reload. Add the suit 350 refit before the Basin exit; Dart 180 already reaches the first shelf, so do not invent a hull350 requirement for 175 m stock. Later deeper Basin work can justify Dart 350. Keep a quiet route and an exposed faster route, plus a dependable refuge and a complete Dart rescue path. This is one full batch, not separate acceptance for each asset.

**Resolve geometry before decorating the problem.** Compare physical `terrainHeight`, its actual float32 rendered triangles, actor support/clearance, camera near plane and `aimRay`/host LOS along ordinary approaches. Source positions currently influence the global heightfield: adding a node can change collision, not just spawn loot. Reuse shared bounds for solid cover, facility openings, dry volumes and resource work faces. The old island-only refinement in [terrainSurface][terrain] is not a general world solution.

For OS2-04, distinguish a camera/mesh intersection from a correctly visible but featureless slope. Fix approximation/support or local material relief accordingly. A proposed camera offset must be root-approved and shared with targeting/view origin; verify near-plane corners, steep slopes, waterline, walking, cockpit and carrier entry. Preserve independently defined airway/pressure datums. No unswept push, automatic pitch or render-only camera lift assumed to be physics-neutral. At steep down-look require readable local relief/contact and recovery of orientation on looking up, not an impossible horizon in every downward view.

For OS2-06, author geography within the actual viewing/response distances. At the historical 53 m lane, cover tops out at 73 m depth in the current descriptor: a warning must not imply immediately usable cover that is below/out of view. Either supply a genuinely reachable retreat/cover approach or reconcile the encounter trigger with the visible descent; test the resulting travel/air cost. Use crown/rib/dish silhouettes, brighter water above darker depth bands and localized silt, retaining atmosphere. Do not globally remove fog. A hunter may remain occluded: visible warning anatomy/wake belongs to the actual animal; a brief call-origin effect belongs to the copied emission position and expires. Preserve acoustic bearing/elevation/captions when unseen; never draw through walls or convert the cue into live tracking. Keep known-place markers and undiscovered regional leads distinct.

| Matched playable-view scene | Acceptance question |
| --- | --- |
| Existing 53 m Canopy approach, then descent toward 90–130 m | Before commitment, can the player point to a clear return, a real shelter/cover approach and the laboratory landmark? Compare quiet transit, first warning and disengagement with actual mode/origin telemetry. No text-only counterplay in an empty field. |
| Lab approach from exposed and sheltered sides; source work face before/after depletion | Does visible entrance/stock match collision, air and E/Q reach? Inspect at 25/50/80 m approach samples, then 4–8 m preview and <4 m action. Distance samples are trials, not promised visibility through all water. |
| Floor contacts at reef controls, Canopy source slope and Basin silt ridge | Repeat downward swimming and backing out at matched poses/pitches; no mesh penetration/flat wash hiding every spatial cue, no false interaction bracket through ground. Preserve the stage1 surfacing regression. |
| Basin dish crest → two sediment lanes → shelter/return fork | Landmark/rule/source/reward are distinguishable; disturbance visibly corresponds to the authored rule. No invisible world-edge stop on the intended route. Beyond it, readable terrain/edge feedback permits turning back. |
| Dart cockpit at 960×600 and 1280×800; later carrier approach with a deployed craft | Compare the same seat/FOV/heading, quality and HUD states. Reduce the cream console's dominance with material/shape changes first; retain real gauges, glass/occlusion and enough view of cover/destination. Test dense warnings without hiding the immediate action. |

Bind comparisons to source/build, save hash, pose, simulation tick, viewport/DPR/quality and renderer. Importing an earned checkpoint is a continuation; seeded carrier/performance scenes are diagnostics. Ordinary-control outbound/return/failure runs are additionally required. **No browser, server or new visual test was used for this advisory task.** Future authorized browser briefs must first read `/work/repos/fleet/BROWSER_RULES.md` when available and `docs/BROWSER_RULES.md`, verify isolation and close only their own resources.

Measure flora/fauna/silt/landmarks **and carrier visible** before detailed fleet furnishing. The initial carrier scene may reuse a clearly labelled fixture; repeat with an earned carrier after the fleet batch. Quality should reduce secondary detail/particles before it removes cover, source hosts or navigation. No software-rendered capture qualifies dedicated-GPU acceptance.

Pin a live encounter/recovery/transfer until its defined completion or disengagement; otherwise suspend regional behavior explicitly without a surprise reset on re-entry. Test region re-entry, save/reload while remote from a wreck, replacement sessions and graphics reconstruction.

## 6. Save compatibility and physical recovery dependencies

Propose **schema 3 / next expedition content version** for changed state shape; root chooses exact tags after stage1. Do not implement migration in this advisory task. Current schema 2/`expedition.3`, schema 2/`expedition.2`, schema 1/`foundation.1` and valid carrier fixtures remain readable through explicit versioned paths.

1. Validate an old envelope against its **old closed domain**, then migrate and strictly validate the new state. Current checks compare all source IDs, exactly four facilities, evidence provenance text, fixed capacities and Dart-only campaign ownership: using expanded registries to validate old data first would reject legitimate saves. Freeze the needed historical definitions; do not loosen validation to arbitrary IDs/fields. Future/corrupt imports still refuse without writes.
2. Initialize newly introduced sources/sites once by stable ID; never refill old stock/reserves or redo repaired facilities. Preserve item/container/module/frame-investment IDs, charge, damage, bound repair provenance, food/grace, blueprints, evidence/ticks, scans, journals, markers and recovery caches. Keep previously paid recipe receipts without refunds/rebilling. Legacy trim stays installed with its existing 2-CU accounting; the ECO draft's zero-CU fitted rule is not authority to rewrite it.
3. Convert static refuge IDs explicitly; do not auto-register a new mobile home. Preserve valid berth/capture/launch phases, transaction IDs and independent craft state. Extend campaign ownership legally without laundering fixtures into earned games. Where capacity rules change, retain the old valid load or require a supported explicit conversion; never silently eject cargo.
4. Expand horizontal **and vertical** bounds together: validator currently restricts Y to −200..100 and vectors to ±1000. Audit terrain sampling, physical queries, source-generated ledges, rendering extents, interaction distances and carrier child/yaw/exit bounds. Preserve old safe poses; any unavoidable compatibility relocation must be deterministic, bounded, fully clear, visible and idempotent, with no grants or passage through sealed structures. Stage1 owns its pending trap solution; do not duplicate or override it here.
5. Test foundation/expedition 2/expedition 3 earned exports, installed trim, depleted sources, multiple losses, near-edge carrier/local poses and prepared/lock transitions. Migration→encode→decode is stable; every successful paused command is immediately saveable. Keep atomic current/previous journal, exclusive writer, cancellation, protected imports and explicit unsaved play unchanged. Measure expanded saves against the 1 MiB cap before changing limits.

**Recovery is a world-authoring prerequisite.** For each loss-capable site record starter route to staging, local operator refuge, complete tether guide and clearance, accessible exterior collar, tow envelope/turns, safe mooring **or** salvage-canister path, and ordinary/advanced cargo disposition. Test every segment and endpoint, not just depth reach. Bobbin remains shallow-built/reusable and pod-rechargeable, with no passenger, bulk mining or story-machine operation; its camera may retain legitimately observed facts. No live remote service, world-wide summon or second upgraded duplicate hull is needed.

Carrier loss adds attached vessels, installed furniture/modules and containers to the conservation problem. Resolve occupied recovery safely before moving an assembly; never salvage an occupied parent or orphan its berths. If the large hull cannot clear the route, recover advanced modules/frame investment and cargo physically in canisters, then rebuild from that recovered investment. A disabled registered cabin/carrier must not grant infinite safe respawn air: validate health, power/emergency supply, habitat/service state, clear landing and exit, and fall back to the pod if unsafe. Exercise registration, safe return and unsafe loss through campaign controls, not only an incapacity fixture.

Retain [ECO-01][eco] as a proposal and [check-economy.mjs](check-economy.mjs) as its arithmetic evidence. The [M1 runtime checker](../../../scripts/check-m1-economy.mjs) uses staged positions and real transactions, not route play. Import approved values into the sole runtime registry in the batch that uses them; recompute the full ledger with M1's changed starter recipes and optional 2-crust/2-resin trim rather than copying the old campaign totals.

| Reach before protection | ≤150 m Canopy supplies 350; ceramic 250–285/core 280–320 are reached with 350; lattice 360–390 with 450 personal and adequate hull (carrier 400 is sufficient for the outer ledges). Blueprint, bench, exit and return must all precede the upgrade. First stock cannot need its own heat/brine protection. |

Candidate worst carrier branch leaves only 3 glass/4 membrane/4 safe-shelf lattice; these are **draft** margins. | Carrier effort and hauling | Draft 106 CU raw carrier stock, 16 tagged alloy from two Basin frame patches, proposed 40/34/32-CU complementary loads. Validate the reusable 24-CU buoy and starter/Creel alternatives with actual transfers/clearance. Substantial investment must coincide with investigations, not repeated trips to one heap. |
| Loadout and final repair | Draft Creel rack 96/cabin 40/service 52 CU, Mantle 52 CU and final 48-CU load are **not runtime capacities**. Current fixture Creel is 64; other fallback hull holds are 32. Check module packing, the installed-trim exception, service-pallet fit, one-mount exchange, spare power/food and underwater exits. Draft final ingredients are 7/3/7/5/1/4/2/3 in A/G/M/C/R/P/T/B order, plus ordinary spares; re-price with real transactions. |
| First deep visit versus final return | Draft exterior District repair 13 CU plus 16 CU reserves precedes the final 48-CU return. Its bench/charging must work on the Creel path and cannot substitute for independently carried final machinery air/power. Include all suit 800/seal costs. |
| Oxygen/power margins | Ordinary conservative first visits should return with ≥25% oxygen/power at the relevant **pre-refill** checkpoints. Capture sortie minima, delivered cargo and recharge use; full air on boarding cannot hide an unsafe diver leg. Current generic non-Dart drain and Hush/Mantle handling are not the draft endurance proof. |
| Repeated failure | Disable every advanced hull, empty ordinary pockets, deplete batteries and block a hatch. Start with retained tools/shallow stock, obtain/use the reusable kit, retrieve critical modules and advanced frame materials, then rebuild/service without inaccessible new stock. Maintenance-bound material never becomes public spending; compare totals across repeated failures/reloads. |
| Food and friction | Runtime 70 food / 35 active minutes is a rule, not tested meal pacing; preserve grace, immediate shallow staples, no thirst/spoilage/farming requirement. Count collection, transfer, refit, empty travel and repeated hauling in actual runs. Shorten routes/improve useful payloads when these replace decisions. |

## 8. Acceptance and continuation

Every implemented batch, including art/lore, receives author checks, root artifact inspection and **independent non-author Astra xhigh plus Sol6.1/max review of one frozen full-batch SHA**. Related leaves share that gate; no review per trivial leaf and no uncovered leaf. Corrections go back to both reviewers with original scope, prior findings/dispositions and updated evidence. Integrated M2 receives a separate milestone gate. At stage exit root can use all four slots for itself and the pair plus **Opus5.5/high**; initial reviews remain independent. Follow [delivery](../../DELIVERY_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md) and [stage protocol](../tasks/OPUS-STAGE-REVIEWS.md), including detailed advice, Sol corrections and fresh Opus verification of substantive findings.

M2 must demonstrate, on the actual production build:

- All seven regions/three islands connected with source/capability/recovery routes; the Canopy–Basin benchmark visibly passes OS2-04/06 before breadth.
- Ordinary-control New Game→ending for Creel/service stops (including a Creel-first route without Dart) and carrier/Mantle, with no requirement to buy Hush/Spindle/every module or read optional logs. Hearthline arrives with substantial campaign use remaining; measured acquisition timing is reported, not assumed midcampaign by recipe count.
- All six hulls obtainable and their basic roles actually usable; early refuge/loadout investment remains useful. Record mission smoke evidence now; M3 owns full authored niche acceptance and fresh-player preference evidence.
- Earned carrier habitation/registration, dry Spindle during another launch, surface-only Spindle deployment, two-compact/one-medium limits, blocked exits and interrupted/save-loaded transfers with exactly-once cargo/hull identity. No claim of underway walking.
- Safe/unsafe registered-refuge loss, food from empty inventory, personal-versus-hull exposure, all-advanced-disabled deep recovery, blocked-hatch salvage and repeated failure; each newly hazardous site has a demonstrated recovery route.
- Essential facts retained out of order/across incapacity/reload, missing optional records tolerated, legal machinery transitions and a resolved ending. Public labels/PRs remain spoiler-safe; internal checks use the appendix.
- Legacy-save matrix, region activation/disposal/re-entry, actual second-session reload, pause/focus/context-loss and bounded performance evidence, with exact source/build/provenance.

**M3:** complete all C01–C15 physical/alternate placements and contextual interpretations, the three independent foreshadow channels, fuller opening/middle/ending, distinctive hull missions, inhabited assets, ecological/source behaviors and audio. Re-run both routes as affected, then paired milestone review and Opus stage 3. No required feature is waived merely because M2 used rough presentation.

**M4:** commission the fresh dedicated non-author **Astra xhigh game-design critic after M3**, early enough for Sol fixes and focused re-review ([critic brief](../tasks/DESIGN-CRITIC.md)). Complete controls/accessibility, economy/route tuning, audible mix, persistence and dedicated-GPU profiling; run final normal-input completion/recovery/second-session checks, the final independent pair and Opus stage 4 with correction loops. Root handles authorized feature branches/PRs; this advisory task creates none.

Evidence exceptions remain explicit: seeded carrier/geometry probes prove bounded mechanics, not earned campaign completion; synthetic input does not prove physical-mouse comfort; muted captures do not prove audio quality. **Fresh-human ten-hour duration/enjoyment, route learning, mystery comprehension and representative dedicated-GPU performance remain unverified until measured.** Model reviews cannot supply those results. Qualified delivery may retain the documented human/hardware exceptions; missing functional endings, rescue routes or blocking defects are not such exceptions.
